about: Token prices GrantBridge uses to estimate the cost of each AI call. Rates are US dollars per 1 million tokens. Edit this file, or point GRANTBRIDGE_PRICING_FILE at another one, when prices change. A model with no entry here gets no cost estimate: GrantBridge never guesses a price.

models.source: OpenAI API pricing, gpt-6-luna, Standard tier

also_checked.finding: Same rates on the model page: input $0.1, cached input $0.01, cache writes $0.125, output $0.5 per 1M tokens. Cached input is 10% of the input rate; cache writes are 1.25x; prompts over 272K input tokens cost 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output for the whole request; regional processing adds 10%.

For GPT-5.6 and later, a 30-minute cache write costs 1.25x the uncached input rate and a cache read 0.1x. cached_tokens (reads) and cache_write_tokens are both parts of input_tokens: ordinary input = input_tokens - cached_tokens - cache_write_tokens.
Reasoning tokens are billed as output tokens. They are included in output_tokens.

Lists GPT-6 Luna (Global and Data Zone) with every price shown as '$-': 'GPT-6 Sol and Luna prices are currently in processing for publishing on this page.' So OpenAI's list price is the only published rate.

models.route: The course PORTKEY_API_KEY sends gpt-6-luna to Azure OpenAI, global deployment (response model gpt-6-luna-global, served model gpt-6-luna-2026-09-22, region East US 2, pay-as-you-go), seen in response headers on 2026-10-20. Global deployments use the global list price, so no regional uplift is applied.
notes: cache_write is the 30-minute write rate, the default cache lifetime. GrantBridge never asks for 12-hour writes ($0.25 per 1M).
The second tier applies to the whole request when it has more than 272,000 input tokens. GrantBridge prompts stay far below that.
A Portkey response-cache hit is a saved copy of an earlier identical answer. The request never reaches Azure, so GrantBridge counts its cost as $0.
